name: indexByRow
title: Translates matrix indices by rows into indices by columns

origin.description: Translates matrix indices by rows into indices by columns.

arguments.name: dim
arguments.text: A numeric vector of length two specifying the length of the "template" matrix.

arguments.name: idxs
arguments.text: A vector indicating subset of elements to operate over. If NULL, no subsetting is done.

origin.details: The current implementation does not support long-vector indices, because both input and output indices are of type integers. This means that the indices in argument idxs can only be in range [1,2^31-1]. Using a greater value will be coerced to NA_integer_. Moreover, returned indices can only be in the same range [1,2^31-1].
origin.value: Returns an integer vector of indices.
origin.example:
dim <- c(5, 4)
X <- matrix(NA_integer_, nrow = dim[1], ncol = dim[2])
Y <- t(X)
idxs <- seq_along(X)

# Assign by columns
X[idxs] <- idxs
print(X)

# Assign by rows
Y[indexByRow(dim(Y), idxs)] <- idxs
print(Y)

stopifnot(X == t(Y))

translation.description: Translates matrix indices by rows into indices by columns.

arguments.name: dim
arguments.text: Two numbers giving the template matrix, nrow then ncol. The matrix is stored column-major, as in R. A two-dimensional array is the defunct matrix form.

arguments.name: idxs
arguments.text: 1-based indexes in row-major order. None visits every cell. Zero and negative values are errors. Numeric values are truncated toward zero. A value outside the 32-bit integer range becomes an integer NA, which the index check rejects.

translation.details: The indexbyrow crate ports matrixStats src/indexByRow.c. None walks the template in row-major order and returns the 1-based column-major position of each cell, in that visit order. A supplied idxs vector is the same row-major numbering and is returned in the same order, duplicates included. This routine does not call validateIndices, so a negative index is an error rather than an exclusion. Indexes and the returned positions stay inside [1, 2^31-1]. The product of dim is rejected when it is larger than 2^31-1; the message prints that product as a double, matching the C check.
translation.value: A one-dimensional int32 array of indexes, in the requested order.
translation.example:
from matrixstats.indexbyrow import indexByRow

dim = (5, 4)
indexByRow(dim)
